title: Multi-Agent Collaboration, Swarms & Supervisors
description: Architect specialized multi-agent teams using supervisor-worker hierarchies, handoffs, and consensus patterns in .NET.

data.text: Single Agent vs Multi-Agent: When to Divide and Conquer

A common anti-pattern is attempting to build a 'god agent'—a single system prompt with 30 distinct tools, 50 rules, and multiple competing objectives. As tool count and prompt size grow, LLMs experience 'tool confusion' (selecting the wrong function), context window dilution, and instruction degradation. Multi-agent systems solve this by decomposing large problem domains into focused, specialized roles: a legal reviewer, a data analyst, an editor, coordinated by a supervisor.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Avoid 'god agents': divide complex domains into focused, specialized agent roles
The Supervisor pattern provides controlled, deterministic governance over worker agents
Keep agent communication channels bounded to prevent exponential token inflation
Ensure each worker agent possesses only the specific tools required for its narrow responsibility
Use handoffs for pipeline workflows and supervisor routing for multi-domain triage
data.takeaway: Multi-agent systems provide modularity, higher reasoning accuracy, and reduced tool hallucination by distributing complex enterprise workflows among focused specialist agents.
